u8eeafc83dc: Off: the tool cannot communicate with the PC, so none of the following operations work; the serial port cannot be used either.
u94bf12cc29: Switch 7 on: the tool initializes its USB function, can act as a serial port tool and can receive commands from the PC.

u0b0100c900: Switch 5 on: DP and DM on the tool's output are used for the serial port function by default.

u6b1d3c2488: TX used for both transmit and receive
u575a7156d7: TX used for both transmit and receive. In addition, when the baud rate is set to 9600 or less, TX sends uartkey. (Currently used for chips that support single-wire UART upgrade)
ue81a0974d9: When the tool receives a JTAG operation command from the PC: DP and DM on the tool's output are used for JTAG communication.
u055f3c2808: When the tool receives an upgrade command from the PC: equivalent to pressing the upgrade button; the tool enters the upgrade process.

u0017e64e9c: Building the SDK with Code::Blocks on Windows is sometimes slow. The possible reasons are as follows:
u6262d7cf83: Antivirus software is installed, but not all executables under the ⟦1⟧C:\JL⟦/1⟧ directory (recursively, including all subdirectories) are trusted. As a result, each time the compiler is called, the antivirus software intercepts and scans the process, which slows the build down. ⟦2⟧We recommend turning off the antivirus software or trusting this directory⟦/2⟧.
u4a19dc548b: Code::Blocks may be an older version that does not support parallel builds. We recommend updating to the ⟦1⟧latest stable version of Code::Blocks (click here to download)⟦/1⟧.
ue1b7ca2a4a: Compiler warning options such as ⟦1⟧-Wundef⟦/1⟧ may be enabled in the SDK without the warnings having been eliminated in the SDK, which produces a lot of compiler output and slows the build down. Consider removing these options as follows:
u1139d1e5e7: Proceed in the same way for the other options. Note also that some options are in Other compiler options
uee71ef563f: In some cases, the built files (that is, sdk.elf and app.bin) turn out to be different, for example, the file size or the checksum has changed. There are several possible reasons for this.
ube1ce8f488: The same project produces different files
u5f121512e5: In some cases, the same project (that is, the same cbp project or the same Makefile project) produces different files.
u4e43a5a55c: The project settings (compiler flags, etc.), the library (.a) files, the link order of the files, etc., or the source files themselves have been modified
u9b18d9c339: The source code in the project uses time-related macros such as ⟦1⟧__DATE__⟦/1⟧ and ⟦2⟧__TIME__⟦/2⟧
